title: Persistence & Data Model Hardening
brief: BLOCKING first milestone for the Business Management track. Wires all 9 unpersisted business engines to PersistenceBridge so data survives server restarts. Enhances Employee, JobTimeEntry, and ShiftEntry data models with HR and production-quality fields. Fixes the /job-time-pause routing bug, adds missing dispatcher actions, strips .passthrough() from schemas, adds secondary indexes for O(1) active job lookups, and applies XSS sanitization to all user text inputs.

phases.title: Persistence, Data Models & Route Hardening
phases.description: Wire all 9 un-persisted business engines to PersistenceBridge, enhance Employee/JobTimeEntry/ShiftEntry models with production-quality HR and lean-manufacturing fields, create DB migrations, fix the /job-time-pause routing bug, add missing dispatcher actions, remove .passthrough() from schemas, add secondary in-memory indexes for O(1) active job lookups, and apply XSS sanitization to all user-supplied text fields.

units.title: Wire PayrollEngine to PersistenceBridge

steps.instruction: Read PayrollEngine.ts in full to identify all in-memory Maps (payroll_periods, pay_stubs, deduction_configs, ytd_earnings) and all mutating methods
Import persistenceBridge from src/db/PersistenceBridge.ts at the top of PayrollEngine.ts

In the PayrollEngine constructor, call persistenceBridge.register('payroll_periods', this.payrollPeriods), register('pay_stubs', this.payStubs), register('deduction_configs', this.deductionConfigs), register('ytd_earnings', this.ytdEarnings)
Add await persistenceBridge.persist('payroll_periods') at the end of createPeriod()
Add await persistenceBridge.persist('pay_stubs') at the end of calculatePayStub()
Add await persistenceBridge.persist('deduction_configs') at the end of configureDeductions()
Add await persistenceBridge.persist('ytd_earnings') wherever ytd_earnings Map is mutated
Open BusinessStore.ts and add ENTITY_CONFIGS entries for payroll_periods, pay_stubs, deduction_configs, ytd_earnings with correct knownColumns and jsonColumns
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Manual smoke test: create a payroll period, restart the server process, verify period is still present

deliverables.description: PayrollEngine with PersistenceBridge registration and persist() calls
ENTITY_CONFIGS updated with payroll entity entries

exit_conditions: payroll_periods, pay_stubs, deduction_configs, ytd_earnings Maps are registered with PersistenceBridge
persist() is called in createPeriod(), calculatePayStub(), configureDeductions()
Server restart preserves all payroll data
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
knowledge_sources: src/engines/EmployeeEngine.ts (reference — already wired, use as pattern)
abort_criteria: PersistenceBridge API has changed and register() signature is incompatible — escalate to lead
PayrollEngine has no in-memory Maps (data stored elsewhere) — re-read and re-plan

units.title: Wire remaining 8 engines to PersistenceBridge

steps.instruction: For each of the 8 engines below, read the file, identify all in-memory Maps, import persistenceBridge, register each Map in the constructor, and add persist() calls at the end of every mutating method. Engines: HRComplianceEngine.ts, ActualCostEngine.ts, OEECalculatorEngine.ts, QualityManagementEngine.ts, OrderManagerEngine.ts, JobLifecycleEngine.ts, QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts, ApprovalWorkflowEngine.ts
HRComplianceEngine: register compliance_records, training_records, incident_reports (or equivalent Maps). Add persist() in recordIncident(), completeTraining(), acknowledgePolicy()
ActualCostEngine: register cost_entries, cost_summaries Maps. Add persist() in recordCost(), closePeriod()
OEECalculatorEngine: register oee_records, downtime_events Maps. Add persist() in recordDowntime(), calculateShiftOEE()
QualityManagementEngine: register quality_events, ncr_records, inspection_results Maps. Add persist() in recordDefect(), createNCR(), closeInspection()
OrderManagerEngine: register orders, order_lines Maps. Add persist() in createOrder(), updateOrderStatus(), shipOrder()
JobLifecycleEngine: register jobs, job_events Maps. Add persist() in createJob(), transitionJob(), closeJob()
QuoteAnalyticsEngine: register quotes, quote_line_items Maps. Add persist() in createQuote(), updateQuote(), convertQuote()
ApprovalWorkflowEngine: register approval_requests, approval_decisions Maps. Add persist() in submitRequest(), approve(), reject()
Add ENTITY_CONFIGS entries in BusinessStore.ts for every newly registered entity (knownColumns + jsonColumns for any object-valued fields)
Run npm run build:fast and fix any type errors before proceeding
Verify all 15 business engines now have PersistenceBridge wiring by grepping for 'persistenceBridge.register' in each engine file

deliverables.description: Persistent HR compliance records
Persistent actual cost entries
Persistent OEE and downtime events
Persistent quality events and NCRs
Persistent orders and order lines
Persistent job lifecycle events
Persistent quote analytics
Persistent approval workflow state
ENTITY_CONFIGS updated for all 8 engines

exit_conditions: All 15 business engines have at least one persistenceBridge.register() call in their constructor
All mutating methods call persist() for the Map they modify
BusinessStore.ts ENTITY_CONFIGS covers every registered entity name
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
grep 'persistenceBridge.register' in each of the 8 engine files returns at least 1 match
knowledge_sources: src/engines/PayrollEngine.ts (completed in U-BIZ01 — use as pattern)
abort_criteria: An engine stores data in PostgreSQL directly (not in-memory Maps) — skip PersistenceBridge for that engine and document why
More than 3 type errors from a single engine edit — revert that engine and treat it separately

rollback.procedure: git checkout -- src/engines/HRComplianceEngine.ts src/engines/ActualCostEngine.ts src/engines/OEECalculatorEngine.ts src/engines/QualityManagementEngine.ts src/engines/OrderManagerEngine.ts src/engines/JobLifecycleEngine.ts src/engines/QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts src/engines/ApprovalWorkflowEngine.ts src/db/BusinessStore.ts

units.title: Job time tracking model enhancements + migration 012

steps.instruction: Read TimeClockEngine.ts in full. Identify the JobTimeEntry interface, ShiftEntry interface, jobPause(), jobStop(), clockOut() method signatures

Add to JobTimeEntry interface: process_type: 'setup' | 'run' | 'inspection' | 'rework' | 'teardown' (if absent); pause_periods: Array<{ started_at: string; resumed_at: string | null; reason: string; reason_category: PauseReasonCategory }> (if absent, default []); good_parts: number (if absent, default 0); scrap_count: number (if absent, default 0); scrap_reason: string | undefined; improvement_note: string | undefined; takt_time_sec: number | undefined
Define PauseReasonCategory as: type PauseReasonCategory = 'material_wait' | 'machine_down' | 'tooling' | 'quality_hold' | 'personal' | 'meeting' | 'other'

Enhance jobPause(jobId, reason, reasonCategory) to accept reason: string and reason_category: PauseReasonCategory parameters. Push a new pause period object to pause_periods with started_at = now, resumed_at = null, reason, reason_category. Call persist() after mutation
Enhance jobResume(jobId) to find the last pause_period with resumed_at = null and set resumed_at = now. Call persist() after mutation
Enhance jobStop(jobId, params: { good_parts: number; scrap_count: number; scrap_reason?: string }) to accept production count params, store them on the entry, and call persist() after mutation
Add getActiveAndPausedJobs(employeeId): JobTimeEntry[] method that returns entries for the employee where status is 'active' or 'paused' and shift is still open
Add handoff_notes: string | undefined field to ShiftEntry interface
Enhance clockOut(shiftId, handoffNotes?: string) to accept optional handoff_notes and store on the ShiftEntry. Call persist() after mutation
Add getShiftHandoff(employeeId): { shift: ShiftEntry; activeJobs: JobTimeEntry[] } | null method that returns the current open shift plus all active/paused jobs for handoff display

Create src/db/migrations/012-job-time-enhancements.sql with: ALTER TABLE job_time_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS process_type VARCHAR(20), ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pause_periods JSONB DEFAULT '[]', ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS good_parts INTEGER DEFAULT 0, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scrap_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scrap_reason VARCHAR(500), ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS improvement_note VARCHAR(500), ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS takt_time_sec NUMERIC(10,2); ALTER TABLE shift_entries ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS handoff_notes VARCHAR(500); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_job_time_entries_process_type ON job_time_entries (process_type); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_job_time_entries_status_employee ON job_time_entries (employee_id, status) WHERE status IN ('active', 'paused')

Update BusinessStore.ts ENTITY_CONFIGS.job_time_entries: add process_type, scrap_reason, improvement_note to knownColumns; add pause_periods to jsonColumns. Update shift_entries ENTITY_CONFIGS: add handoff_notes to knownColumns
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

deliverables.description: Enhanced time tracking with pause reasons, production counts, process_type, handoff support
Job time and shift entry schema migration
ENTITY_CONFIGS updated for enhanced job time and shift entries

ShiftEntry has handoff_notes
jobPause() accepts reason + reason_category and appends to pause_periods
jobResume() closes the open pause period with resumed_at timestamp
jobStop() stores good_parts, scrap_count, scrap_reason
getActiveAndPausedJobs(employeeId) returns correct entries
getShiftHandoff(employeeId) returns shift + job list
clockOut() stores handoff_notes
Migration 012 applies cleanly
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors

units.title: Fix route bug + add missing dispatcher actions

steps.instruction: Read src/routes/erp.ts and find the POST /job-time-pause route. Verify it currently calls timeClockEngine.jobStart() (or job_time_start handler) instead of jobPause(). Fix it to call timeClockEngine.jobPause(params.job_id, params.reason, params.reason_category)
Read businessDispatcher.ts and locate the z.enum action list (approx line 346). Check whether 'job_time_pause' and 'job_time_resume' are already present. If absent, add them to the enum
In businessDispatcher.ts, add or verify case 'job_time_pause': calls timeClockEngine.jobPause(args.job_id, args.reason, args.reason_category) and returns the updated entry
In businessDispatcher.ts, add or verify case 'job_time_resume': calls timeClockEngine.jobResume(args.job_id) and returns the updated entry

Read businessActionSchemas.ts and add or verify schema for job_time_pause with fields: job_id (string required), reason (string required), reason_category (z.enum PauseReasonCategory values required). Add schema for job_time_resume with field: job_id (string required). Ensure neither schema uses .passthrough()
Add 'employee_update' to z.enum in businessDispatcher.ts if absent. Add case 'employee_update': calls employeeEngine.update(args.employee_id, args) and returns the updated employee
Add 'who_clocked_in_live' to z.enum in businessDispatcher.ts if absent. Add case 'who_clocked_in_live': calls timeClockEngine.getActiveEmployees() (or equivalent) and returns the list
Scan businessActionSchemas.ts for any remaining .passthrough() calls and remove them all
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Manually test the /job-time-pause route: POST to it with job_id + reason, verify it calls jobPause (not jobStart)

deliverables.description: /job-time-pause route fixed to call jobPause()

units.title: Input sanitization + secondary in-memory indexes

steps.instruction: Read TimeClockEngine.ts. Check if a sanitizeText() helper already exists (either in this file or in src/utils/). If not present in utils, create it in src/utils/sanitize.ts: export function sanitizeText(raw: string, maxLen = 500): string — strips HTML tags via regex /<[^>]*>/g, trims whitespace, enforces maxLen, and throws a 400-class error (or returns '') if the input matches /<script|onerror|javascript:/i patterns
Import sanitizeText in TimeClockEngine.ts
Apply sanitizeText() to handoff_notes before storing in clockOut()
Apply sanitizeText() to the pause reason string before pushing to pause_periods in jobPause()
Apply sanitizeText() to scrap_reason and improvement_note before storing in jobStop() and any setImprovementNote() method

Add two secondary indexes as private Maps in TimeClockEngine: activeJobsByEmployee: Map<string, Set<string>> mapping employee_id -> Set<job_entry_id> for status='active'; pausedJobsByEmployee: Map<string, Set<string>> mapping employee_id -> Set<job_entry_id> for status='paused'
Populate both indexes on engine initialization by iterating the job_time_entries Map

Keep indexes in sync: add to activeJobsByEmployee when a job becomes active (jobStart), move from active to paused index on jobPause(), move from paused to active index on jobResume(), remove from both indexes on jobStop()
Update getActiveAndPausedJobs(employeeId) to use the secondary indexes instead of iterating all entries — O(1) lookup via activeJobsByEmployee.get(employeeId) and pausedJobsByEmployee.get(employeeId)
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
Write a quick sanity check: create 3 jobs for an employee, pause 2, verify getActiveAndPausedJobs returns all 3 in correct states using the index path

deliverables.description: sanitizeText() helper: HTML strip, max length, XSS rejection
sanitizeText() applied to all user text fields; O(1) secondary indexes for active/paused jobs by employee

exit_conditions: sanitizeText() exists and strips <script>, onerror, javascript: patterns
handoff_notes, pause reason, scrap_reason, improvement_note all go through sanitizeText() before storage
activeJobsByEmployee and pausedJobsByEmployee Maps exist in TimeClockEngine
getActiveAndPausedJobs() uses index lookup, not full Map iteration
Indexes stay in sync through jobStart/jobPause/jobResume/jobStop lifecycle
npm run build:fast produces 0 errors
knowledge_sources: src/utils/ (check for existing sanitize helpers before creating new ones)
abort_criteria: A sanitize utility already exists in src/utils/ — import and use it rather than creating a duplicate

forge_triple.hook: biz-persistence-guard — warns on engine edits to any business engine file when that engine has no persistenceBridge.register() call, blocking commit until persistence is wired
forge_triple.action: prism_business:biz_persistence_status — enumerates all 15 business engines, reports which have PersistenceBridge wiring, which Maps are registered, and last persist() timestamp per entity
forge_triple.skill: /biz-health — checks business engine persistence health: lists engines missing PersistenceBridge, reports entity count per registered Map, flags any ENTITY_CONFIGS gaps
